test_title: PYST 17: RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I - Mathematics (Held On: 12 Jun, 2025 Shift 2)
subject: maths
question: A tap fills a cistern in 9 hours. Another tap empties the full tank in 90 hours. How long (in hours) will it take to fill twice the volume of the tank, if the tank is empty initially and both the taps are open together?
solution:
**Given:**

Tap A fills the tank in 9 hours

Tap B empties the full tank in 90 hours

We need to find the time to fill 2 tanks when both taps are open together

**Formula used:**

Efficiency = Total work / Time

**Calculation:**

Let the total work = LCM of 9 and 90 = 90 units 

Total work to fill twice the volume of the tank = 2 × 90 = 180 units

Efficiency of A = 90 ÷ 9 = 10 units/hour

Efficiency of B = 90 ÷ 90 = 1 unit/hour (emptying)

Net efficiency = 10 − 1 = 9 units/hour

⇒ Time = 180 ÷ 9 = 20 hours

**∴ The correct answer is 20 hours.**
